items.title: Holman Bill — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewer asks: 'Solo for Alto, which I presume was for Lee, maybe? Please tell us about those two.' The interviewee responds by discussing the 'Invention for Guitar and Trumpet' assignment from Stan Kenton, mentioning Maynard and Sal, but does not confirm or discuss Lee.

ctx.x: Yeah, Boop-boop-de-doop. I just got that title from a rhythm of the bridge. It goes “boop boop-de-doop doo-be-doop doo-be-doop.” So I used that for a title. Stan – I told you he wouldn‟t say “Zoot.” He wouldn‟t go near “Boop-boop-de-doop.” In fact, we played it on several broadcasts from Birdland, and he made me get up and announce it every time.

Let me just backtrack a little bit, because I found in my notes two compositions: Invention for Guitar and Trumpet. The first entry that I saw for that was in September of ‟52. There are several entries. Again, all the live broadcasts. Then, Solo for Alto, which I presume was for Lee, maybe? Please tell us about those two.

The Invention for Guitar and Trumpet was one of the few assignments that Stan gave me at the time. He knew I was interested in lines and counterpoint and things like that. So he took the name of a contrapuntal form, which is the invention. He had Maynard to play high and Sal to play fast, and asked me to write the piece for them. I did. I don‟t like it at all. That‟s probably the worst chart I wrote for Kenton, and it‟s been recorded the most and re-released on this label and that label. It‟s coming back to haunt…
